constants.comment: How long a fetched model list stays good. Long enough that opening the Action tab, changing the model and opening it again is one outbound call; short enough that a new model on OpenRouter shows up the same working day.
constants.name: MODEL_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS

constants.comment: Postgres refuses a `NOTIFY` payload over 8000 bytes, and it refuses it at *send* time — the transaction errors rather than the notification being silently truncated. Callers send deltas small enough that this never trips; it is checked here anyway so a caller that grows its payload finds out from a log line naming the channel, rather than from an exception raised inside a sync that then looks like a scrape failure.
constants.name: MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES

constants.comment: Seconds between reconnect attempts after the listen connection drops.
constants.name: _RECONNECT_DELAY_SECONDS

constants.comment: How long a Summary waits after a failed run, doubling per consecutive failure, capped at a day. **The other half of "a failed run does not disable the schedule."** That rule is right and this is what makes it affordable. `_is_due` stays true forever once the window has passed, and the scheduler ticks every 60 seconds (`AUTO_SUMMARY_JOB_INTERVAL_SECONDS`), so without a damper a Summary whose Key cannot work retries 1,440 times a day — 1,440 failed log rows, 1,440 authenticated calls to a Provider already rejecting them, and an etag bump every minute that re-invalidates the log list for every open client. The likeliest case is not exotic: an Account that had `autoRegenerate` on before BYOK and has not saved a Key yet fails on `AI_KEY_MISSING_DETAIL` every single tick. Backoff rather than a cap, because a cap is the auto-disable wearing a different hat — the Summary would stop for good on a Provider outage that cleared itself. A day is the ceiling because that is roughly how long somebody takes to notice a Key needs re-saving, and the first retry is still a minute away.
constants.name: _RETRY_BACKOFF_MS

constants.comment: The reference-extraction walk's cadence (the harvest tick), at the same page size. That pace ran on staging's ~4.7M-Post corpus without competing with sync. The batch size is the dial, and this is not a second one.
constants.name: POST_LANGUAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS

constants.comment: How often each process writes the Requests it has buffered. A hard kill loses at most this much, the gap the quota ledger already accepts.
constants.name: REQUEST_FLUSH_SECONDS

constants.comment: How often the hourly and daily Request totals are rebuilt, so the Requests tab is at most this far behind.
constants.name: REQUEST_ROLLUP_INTERVAL_SECONDS

constants.comment: Delete expired posts in bounded batches: a backlog can be hundreds of thousands of rows, and materialising them all at once OOM-killed the worker.
constants.name: POST_DELETE_BATCH

constants.comment: Channels collected per retention pass. Each one is a full corpus delete and nothing waits on the queue draining, so the next hourly run takes the rest.
constants.name: COLLECT_LIMIT

constants.comment: Longest `detail` an announcement carries, comfortably under `pg_notify`'s 8000-byte payload cap with room for the rest of the entry.
constants.name: _MAX_DETAIL_CHARS

constants.comment: Attempts one worker runs at once. Each is one Provider stream, waiting on a remote model rather than on this process.
constants.name: GENERATION_CONCURRENCY

constants.comment: How often a running Attempt writes its text so far to its row.
constants.name: FLUSH_SECONDS

constants.comment: How long a watcher waits on notifications before reading the row again, and how long the consumer waits on a ring before sweeping the Lane.
constants.name: WATCH_POLL_SECONDS

constants.comment: Only covers claim-then-archive, which happen in one transaction.
constants.name: _CLAIM_VT_SECONDS

constants.comment: The temperature Generate always used when nobody chose one.
constants.name: DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE

constants.comment: How long the automatic retry of a transient failure waits when the Provider named no Retry-After (SFR-03), and the most it waits when it did.
constants.name: RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS

constants.comment: How long the drain waits for a healthy worker before concluding that every proxy is parked. Only reached when no worker is free *and* none can become free by a release — which is either "everything is busy" (resolved by waiting on the running tasks) or "every proxy is in cooldown" (resolved by giving up and letting the 30-second sweep come back). **Ticket 14's per-proxy wait does not feed into this, and that is a claim worth stating rather than assuming.** Ticket 13's handover asked that if deliberate waits longer than this constant appeared, it be re-derived from them instead of left a literal. They appeared, and the two still do not meet: this bounds the wait for a *free and healthy worker*, and a worker serving a paced fetch is `busy` — not free, not parked. Pacing lengthens the message a worker is already running, which the drain sees through `all_busy()` as ordinary backpressure. Deriving this from `PACE_MAX_MS` would make every empty-queue sweep block for thirty seconds to no purpose. `tests/services/test_adaptive_proxy_wait.py` holds the guard.
constants.name: _NO_HEALTHY_WORKER_WAIT_SECONDS

constants.comment: How many accounts one lane read will interleave between. A bound because each one costs a read: the round-robin below issues one `pgmq.read` per account with work, and a deployment with 200 accounts on one lane should serve 20 of them per pass rather than issue 200 queries to fill ten slots. The accounts it does not reach this pass are reached on the next, because `distinct_due_values` orders by value and the ones it served have had their messages claimed out of the due set.
constants.name: MAX_INTERLEAVED_USERS

constants.comment: How often the paused-lane set is re-read during one drain. See `_LaneBuffers._refresh_pauses` — a drain is not bounded in length, so a snapshot taken at its start can be hours stale.
constants.name: _PAUSE_RECHECK_SECONDS

constants.comment: How long a lane that read empty is left alone before being asked again. Bounds the cost of re-checking the normal tier while a long best-effort backlog drains — the strict-tier rule needs that re-check to be live, and without an interval it would be a query per dispatched message.
constants.name: _EMPTY_LANE_RECHECK_SECONDS

constants.comment: A single prompt is capped so an oversized selection is refused with a clear error rather than silently truncated (the user's explicit choice) or sent on to blow past a model's context window. ~200k tokens is the context limit of many models; tokens are estimated at ~4 chars each.
constants.name: MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS

constants.comment: 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z. An upper bound on every instant and every span, because without one the arithmetic leaves the range PostgreSQL can compare a `bigint` against: a Duration of 10**25 minutes resolves to a start that makes psycopg raise `NumericValueOutOfRange`, and a 500 is the wrong answer to a number a client simply made up. Far past any real corpus, so the only requests it refuses are ones that were never going to work.
constants.name: MAX_INSTANT_MS

constants.comment: A century. The same argument as `MAX_INSTANT_MS`, for the elapsed values.
constants.name: MAX_SPAN_MINUTES

constants.comment: A Live end's reach either way: a century, in ms.
constants.name: _MAX_OFFSET_MS

constants.comment: A Fixed end's reach either way, inside what a `datetime` holds (years 1 to 9999), so an absurd instant is a 422 and never an overflow.
constants.name: _MAX_INSTANT_MS

constants.comment: How many fixed handles one "cited by" or "cites" Condition names: 500 keeps a shared link under the 8 KB request line common proxies accept, and anything larger is a Tag (DFP-05).
constants.name: MAX_CONDITION_HANDLES

constants.comment: How many Seeds one Shared parents / children Condition sends: every follow, or a Channels tab selection, which can be the whole account.
constants.name: MAX_SEEDS

constants.comment: A Channels tab selection can be the whole account; past this, use "every follow".
constants.name: MAX_YOUR_CHANNELS

constants.comment: The most handles one paste may add (DADD).
constants.name: MAX_ADDED_HANDLES

constants.comment: The limit explicitly named Posts had before (ADR-026).
constants.name: MAX_SELECTION_PICKS

constants.comment: How much of a summary's body travels as the list preview. The read cost is unchanged either way — the detoast happens server-side — but four kinds on one page multiplies the *wire* cost, and the list renders a two-line clamp.
constants.name: ARTIFACT_TITLE_CHARS

constants.comment: How stale the worker's view of `cancel_requested` may be, in seconds. Small, because a person pressed Cancel and is watching; not zero, because the alternative is a `Session` per checkpoint per handle. See `_cancelled`.
constants.name: _CANCEL_POLL_SECONDS

constants.comment: How long to wait before re-probing a handle that keeps failing. Doubles per consecutive failure and stops growing at a day: a handle that has failed eight times in a row is probably failing for a reason a tighter loop will not fix, and the sweep should not keep spending proxy lanes on it.
constants.name: RETRY_BACKOFF_BASE_MINUTES

constants.comment: Priority for a row nothing has ranked. Large rather than 0 so a handle enqueued with a real candidate rank always sorts ahead of one that was not.
constants.name: DEFAULT_PROBE_PRIORITY

constants.comment: A manual recheck or refresh jumps the queue. The operator is looking at that row, and one that waited behind a freshly generated report would take minutes. **Negative, so it beats a rank rather than tying with one.** `enqueue_handles` numbers a report's candidates from zero, so at `0` this sorted level with the strongest candidate of the newest report and the tie fell to whichever handle was alphabetically first. `test_recheck_jumps_the_queue` passed on exactly that accident. Ticket 03 gave the constant a second caller — `refresh_entries` — and the property has to hold by construction for both. **A Priority boost can still beat it** (DPF). The drain order is `priority - priority_boost` and nothing else: an Operator who boosts a batch by more than the gap has said that batch matters more, and an exception here would be one more rule to remember about a number they set themselves.
constants.name: RECHECK_PRIORITY

constants.comment: The largest Priority boost either way. `priority` is int4 and the bands sit within a few million of zero, so the difference cannot overflow. With bands 500,000 apart, that leaves two thousand bands of headroom.
constants.name: MAX_PRIORITY_BOOST

constants.comment: Priority for a handle the harvest sweep found in a stored Post (ticket 04). Behind `DEFAULT_PROBE_PRIORITY` and ahead of `REFRESH_PRIORITY`, which is the ladder's own argument applied once more: a handle somebody's report named is worth more than one nobody asked about, and one nobody asked about is still an answer we have never had, which beats re-fetching an answer we hold. **One number for every harvested handle, not a rank**, and that is the fairness mechanism the ticket asks for rather than a shrug. The sweep walks the corpus with a single cursor and no idea who follows what, so the handles it finds arrive in whatever order the Posts did; giving them all one priority makes `dequeue_handles` fall through to its `handle` tiebreak, and an alphabetical order cannot prefer one account's corpus over another's. Ranking them by discovery order would hand the queue to whichever account's Channels the cursor happened to be walking.
constants.name: HARVEST_PRIORITY

constants.comment: Priority for a handle an Operator pasted into the Directory (DADD). Behind `HARVEST_PRIORITY` and ahead of `REFRESH_PRIORITY`. A pasted handle is one we have never had an answer for, which beats re-fetching one we hold; but the Directory's own discoveries go first, and an Operator who wants a paste sooner has the Priority boost. One value for the whole paste, like a harvest, so the drain order within it falls through to `handle`.
constants.name: NAMED_PRIORITY

constants.comment: Priority for an entry that already has an answer and is only going stale. Larger than `DEFAULT_PROBE_PRIORITY`, so a scheduled refresh drains behind every handle nobody has ever looked at: an answer we hold is worth less than one we have never had. Set on the conclusive branch of `record_probe_result` rather than left alone, because a row keeps the rank of whatever first enqueued it — and a handle rechecked once carries `RECHECK_PRIORITY`, which would put a week-old entry at the front of the queue for ever after.
constants.name: REFRESH_PRIORITY

constants.comment: The search document's recipe (`search_text`). Raise it when the recipe changes, and `scripts/backfill_directory_search.py` re-indexes older rows.
constants.name: SEARCH_INDEX_VERSION

constants.comment: Entries re-indexed per statement by retention and the backfill.
constants.name: SEARCH_BATCH

constants.comment: How long a claim stays valid without a heartbeat. This bounds one thing only: how long a **dead** holder blocks its Channel. A live sync renews well inside it (`CHANNEL_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS`), so a deep backfill running for an hour is never at risk of having its claim stolen mid-walk -- which would put a second backward walk into the cursors the first is still writing, the precise interleaving this exists to prevent. Five minutes rather than the visibility timeout's ~2.4 hours, and the difference is the point. The VT decides when a crashed worker's *message* comes back; the lease decides when its *Channel* does. Sizing the lease off the VT would mean a Channel that crashed at 12:00 refusing every sync until 14:24 -- including the ones a person is sitting in front of.
constants.name: CHANNEL_CLAIM_LEASE_SECONDS

constants.comment: Matches `SUMMARY_PROMPT_EXCERPT_CHARS`. The title is the one line that distinguishes this chat from its siblings in a list, not a summary of it.
constants.name: CHAT_TITLE_CHARS

constants.comment: How long a view's total and Language counts, and the Directory's size, are reused. A Directory that grows while it is read moves by a row or two.
constants.name: COUNTS_TTL_SECONDS

constants.comment: A middle Channel past this many links is an aggregator, not a taste: a source citing more than this many Channels, or a target cited by more.
constants.name: AGGREGATOR_LINKS

constants.comment: The most entries Tick all turns into Ticks; above it a view is All matching (ADR-031). The same number as the ticked Seeds a Condition takes.
constants.name: MAX_TICK_ALL

constants.comment: How many citing Posts "Why it's here" quotes; the rest are counted.
constants.name: WHY_LIMIT

constants.comment: How many shared Channels "Why it's here" names per relation; the rest are counted.
constants.name: SHARED_LIMIT

constants.comment: How many Channels each side of the panel's neighbour lists shows.
constants.name: NEIGHBOURS_LIMIT

constants.comment: How many samples a rate needs before it is reported at all. One constant, not a confidence model and not an error bar. A median over three Posts is a number pretending to be a measurement, and without a floor a three-Post Channel outranks a real one in a sort. Below it the raw sample count still shows, so a suppressed rate can explain itself.
constants.name: MIN_SAMPLES

constants.comment: Below this many letters a Post is `UNDETERMINED` without asking the model. One global value rather than one per language (ADR-021): the corpus is a handful of high-resource languages and nobody tunes this from `.env`. ponytail: counts characters, so a full Chinese or Japanese sentence under 20 characters is `und`; weight dense scripts if a CJK Channel ever matters.
constants.name: MIN_LETTERS

constants.comment: The model's top score must reach this, or the Post is `UNDETERMINED`. On the ADR-021 benchmark it kept fastText's mistakes on two-word Posts to 41 of 1,143.
constants.name: MIN_SCORE

constants.comment: How many of a Channel's newest Posts carrying a code decide its Language: enough to outvote a run of forwards-with-comment, few enough that a Channel which switched language is judged on what it publishes now.
constants.name: LANGUAGE_WINDOW

constants.comment: Log list endpoints are viewers, not exports: cap what one request can load.
constants.name: DEFAULT_LOG_PAGE_SIZE

constants.comment: Attempts a media fetch gets. One, meaning no retry ladder at all. `retries=N` is N *attempts*, and the default 8 with a 3s escalating delay is sized for a page fetch, where losing the page loses the sync. Media is not that. An avatar is re-resolved on **every page** of a walk, so the page loop already is the retry, and a thumb is cosmetic. Left at the default, one dead avatar URL cost eight backed-off attempts per page: `tests/api/test_sync_jobs.py` went from 13 seconds to 8 minutes when the avatar cache first moved onto the lane pool, which is what surfaced this. Shared by both image caches rather than spelled twice, because they are twins and `test_image_cache_egress.py` asserts they stay that way.
constants.name: MEDIA_FETCH_RETRIES

constants.comment: The columns `write_references` binds per row. Named here rather than counted from the model, because the statement binds exactly the keys that function builds and a model column it does not set would not be one of them -- the number has to move when *that dict* does.
constants.name: _BOUND_COLUMNS_PER_ROW

constants.comment: Telegram thumbnails are small; anything larger is not one, and reading it into memory unbounded is how a sync run turns into an OOM.
constants.name: _MAX_THUMB_BYTES

constants.comment: Every spread's bar count (`BINS` in `components/Spread.tsx`), so one component draws both.
constants.name: VALUE_BINS

constants.comment: Upper bound on how many posts one prompt assembles. The token budget is the real user-facing limit; this is a generous fetch-safety bound so a pathological scope never materialises a giant result. Like the token cap, exceeding it is a clear error, never a silent truncation. The AI paths assemble *all* posts in scope (not a page) up to these limits — pagination is display-only.
constants.name: MAX_PROMPT_POSTS

constants.comment: The wait a proxy widens to from healthy. Multiplicative widening from zero stays zero, so the first step is additive and every one after it is not.
constants.name: PACE_STEP_MS

constants.comment: What an explicit rejection or a soft block multiplies the wait by.
constants.name: PACE_WIDEN_FACTOR

constants.comment: The ceiling. Also the point at which a further rejection stops meaning "slow down" and starts meaning "this proxy is unusable" — see the module docstring on the top rung.
constants.name: PACE_MAX_MS

constants.comment: Consecutive successes before the wait narrows one step. Narrowing on *every* success would undo a widening as fast as one request, which re-provokes the limit that caused it.
constants.name: PACE_NARROW_AFTER_SUCCESSES

constants.comment: What one narrowing step multiplies the wait by. Gradual on purpose: this is the "narrows it gradually" half of the ticket, and the failure it avoids is an oscillation between the ceiling and zero rather than a convergence.
constants.name: PACE_NARROW_FACTOR

constants.comment: Weight of the newest sample in the per-proxy latency EMA.
constants.name: PACE_LATENCY_EMA_ALPHA

constants.comment: How many samples the EMA needs before drift is allowed to mean anything. The first request through a lane is always "slower than average" when there is no average, and a cold lane must not throttle itself on that.
constants.name: PACE_DRIFT_MIN_SAMPLES

constants.comment: How far above the EMA an attempt must land to count as drift.
constants.name: PACE_DRIFT_RATIO

constants.comment: What drift multiplies the wait by — deliberately smaller than `PACE_WIDEN_FACTOR`. Drift is a symptom with many innocent causes; a 429 is Telegram saying so.
constants.name: PACE_DRIFT_FACTOR

constants.comment: The ceiling drift alone may push the wait to. A rejection can reach `PACE_MAX_MS`; latency cannot. This is what makes "weak signal" a number rather than an adjective — a proxy that is merely slow must not end up throttled as though it were being refused.
constants.name: PACE_DRIFT_MAX_MS

constants.comment: How long `ProxyWorkerPool.acquire` sleeps before re-checking whether a parked worker's proxy has recovered. A release wakes it immediately; this only bounds how long a *cooldown lapsing* takes to notice, which nothing signals.
constants.name: WORKER_WAKE_POLL_SECONDS

constants.comment: How long a fan-out waits for a healthy Slot before giving up on one Channel. **Unbounded is a hang, not patience** (found in review). `_take_free` skips a worker whose proxy is in cooldown, so with every proxy parked `acquire(timeout=None)` waits for ever — and the two fan-outs that take Slots outside the drain had no deadline at all. A bulk follow's three hundred tasks would all park with the row left `running`, the `finally` that charges the ledger never reached; an `auto_summary` walk would never return and, under APScheduler's `max_instances=1`, suppress every later tick. The old `asyncio.Semaphore` always granted, so this is a hazard the Slots introduced. `sync_queue` has always passed a deadline here, for exactly this reason; these two now do too. Sized like one whole fetch rather than like the drain's five seconds, because a cooldown is ten minutes and these callers have no sweep behind them to come back: giving up marks the Channel failed, which a person sees.
constants.name: SLOT_WAIT_SECONDS

constants.comment: Telegram's `sendMessage` text limit, after entity parsing.
constants.name: TELEGRAM_MESSAGE_LIMIT

constants.comment: An allowance of this or less is unlimited. Negative rather than a sentinel object because the setting is an integer an operator types into `.env`, and this is the one value that cannot collide with a real limit — zero already means something specific (decision 18: always best-effort, never blocked).
constants.name: UNLIMITED

constants.comment: The refresh horizon: sync stops refreshing a stored Post's View count at 7 days (ADR-024). A settling age at or past it would call a count Settled that sync could never have observed that old.
constants.name: REFRESH_HORIZON_HOURS

constants.comment: A span between two knots learns its shape from the data only when at least this many pairs cross it; below, it takes the seed's.
constants.name: MIN_PAIRS_PER_SPAN

constants.comment: Rows per delete, each its own transaction, so a backlog never holds one long transaction that pins the vacuum horizon (see `prune_finished_jobs`).
constants.name: REQUEST_DELETE_BATCH

constants.comment: Rows per delete transaction in `prune_finished_jobs`. Bounds transaction length, not memory — see that function.
constants.name: SYNC_JOB_DELETE_BATCH

constants.comment: How many watched-but-not-run jobs this process keeps mirrored. Evicting one costs a row read to rebuild it, never correctness, so a modest cap is free insurance against the mirror becoming a leak: `GET /jobs/sync/{id}` seeds an entry for any job id a client asks about, and nothing about a finished job makes it fall out on its own.
constants.name: MAX_MIRRORED_JOBS

constants.comment: Same bound, same reason, for the cancellation flags. See `_get_cancel_event`.
constants.name: MAX_TRACKED_CANCEL_EVENTS

constants.comment: What the index holds per entry (ADR-027): the newest samples, capped.
constants.name: SAMPLES_INDEXED

constants.comment: The last word typed matches as a prefix from this many characters.
constants.name: PREFIX_FROM

constants.comment: How much text a snippet keeps around its first match.
constants.name: SNIPPET_BEFORE

constants.comment: Bars in a spread.
constants.name: SPREAD_BARS

constants.comment: Matches truncatePreview's default in frontend/src/lib/commands/search-filters.ts.
constants.name: SUMMARY_PROMPT_EXCERPT_CHARS

constants.comment: How long a coalesced request waits before giving up and reporting a skip. **Ticket 12 removed this constant's original reason and it still earns its place, on a different one.** Ticket 11 justified the bound by the waiter holding a slot in the worker's concurrency gate; ticket 12 made the permit releasable (`sync_queue.SyncSlot`), so a waiter now scrapes nobody's slot. What remains is that the waiter's *message* is claimed from PGMQ under a visibility timeout of about 2.4 hours: a waiter that outlasted it would have its own message redelivered and processed a second time while the first was still waiting. And a person is on the other end of the SSE stream, for whom an answer of "still running" beats an open connection. Fifteen minutes is a judgement, not a derivation, and worth naming as such: long enough that an ordinary sync -- seconds to a couple of minutes -- is always ridden rather than skipped, short enough to stay well inside the visibility timeout.
constants.name: COALESCE_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS

constants.comment: How often a waiter re-checks the claim when no notification arrives. Small, because it is only reached when a ring was lost or the holder died, and both of those should resolve in seconds rather than at the next sweep.
constants.name: _COALESCE_POLL_SECONDS

constants.comment: How long after publication a Post's sightings are kept.
constants.name: OBSERVATION_WINDOW_MS

constants.comment: How far ahead the stride controller forecasts, and the span its inflow is measured over.
constants.name: FORECAST_HORIZON_MS

constants.comment: Threads over and above the connection pool, for the `to_thread` calls that open no `Session` at all — `pg_notify` sends, file writes, the Tor control socket. Small on purpose: threads past the connection count are not more parallelism, they are the same queue one layer down.
constants.name: _NON_DB_THREAD_HEADROOM

constants.comment: Rows drawn under the paste; a 100,000-line paste would freeze the popover.
constants.name: SHOWN_ROWS

constants.comment: The floor's default in `services/reach.py`, until the server's arrives.
constants.name: DEFAULT_ESTIMATION_FLOOR_HOURS

constants.comment: Bars in a spread, as many as the server draws.
constants.name: BINS

constants.comment: Six steps at most: 1/729 of the whole spread.
constants.name: MAX_STEPS

constants.comment: How often a Live bound's fields are redrawn against the clock.
constants.name: REDRAW_MS

constants.comment: Rows kept mounted beyond the viewport. Deliberately generous. Beyond smoothing scrolling, it keeps a workable number of cards reachable to anything that locates them by `[data-channel-name]` without scrolling first — which is how the command palette's channel actions and much of the e2e suite find cards.
constants.name: OVERSCAN_ROWS

constants.comment: The server's cap on one paste (`MAX_ADDED_HANDLES`).
constants.name: MAX_ADDED_HANDLES

constants.comment: The server refuses a longer search.
constants.name: SEARCH_MAX

constants.comment: The server's range either way (`MAX_PRIORITY_BOOST`).
constants.name: MAX_BOOST

constants.comment: Posts shown before "Show N more".
constants.name: FIRST_POSTS

constants.comment: How many channels the line names before the "+N".
constants.name: SHOWN_CHANNELS

constants.comment: How long a `g` or a count waits before its next keys show, so a quick gt never flashes them.
constants.name: HINT_DELAY_MS

constants.comment: A card hidden under the workspace's sticky header is not "on screen".
constants.name: HEADER_PX

constants.comment: How near the last loaded photo the viewer asks the feed for its next page.
constants.name: PAGE_AHEAD

constants.comment: Long enough for the second click or tap of a double to arrive before the first one closes the viewer or toggles its controls.
constants.name: DOUBLE_TAP_MS

constants.comment: How far apart, in px, the two taps of a double-tap may land.
constants.name: DOUBLE_TAP_PX

constants.comment: How far one finger must travel at 1x before it steps or closes.
constants.name: SWIPE_PX

constants.comment: About this many labels on the x axis, whatever the range.
constants.name: TICKS

constants.comment: The topic or row a link names, and how long it stays highlighted.
constants.name: FLASH_MS

constants.comment: How much of a draft shows before Show all.
constants.name: PREVIEW_CHARS

constants.comment: Max auto-sync staleness interval (24 hours).
constants.name: AUTO_SYNC_INTERVAL_MAX_MINUTES

constants.comment: Below this width the app lays out for a phone; one number for every "narrow".
constants.name: MOBILE_BREAKPOINT

constants.comment: How long a typed field waits for the next keystroke before committing.
constants.name: DRAFT_COMMIT_MS

constants.comment: The Settling curve is refitted daily and the reach settings change by hand, so an hour-old copy is as good as a fresh one (PFB-03).
constants.name: VIEW_ESTIMATE_STALE_TIME

constants.comment: One server page. Small, because History renders a card per row.
constants.name: ARTIFACT_PAGE_SIZE

constants.comment: The whole Directory's size moves slowly; the server caches it as long.
constants.name: SIZE_STALE_TIME

constants.comment: How long the box waits for typing to stop before the view takes it.
constants.name: SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_MS

constants.comment: How often to re-read the queue while it is draining. Slower than the old sweep's 1.5s because it no longer drives anything — the server probes at its own pace regardless, so this only sets how promptly resolved rows appear.
constants.name: DRAINING_POLL_INTERVAL_MS

constants.comment: How often to re-read the queue while nothing is draining (ticket 04). Five minutes rather than four seconds because of what is on screen in this state: a day's and a week's Request spend, which moves a few times an hour at most, and which nobody is watching tick. The argument the drain predicate makes against polling for `retrying` — do not poll for the life of a tab to observe something that changes a few times a day — applies here in full, and is why this cadence is slow rather than why there is no cadence at all.
constants.name: IDLE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS

constants.comment: How often the scheduler's status is re-read. Was `App`'s `setInterval`.
constants.name: JOBS_STATUS_POLL_MS

constants.comment: The signed-in account's three Budgets (ticket 24). One query behind both the banner and the settings panel, so the two cannot disagree about whether this account is out of Requests. Refetched on an interval, and that is not decoration: the spend changes without the browser doing anything — the scheduler syncs, and the ceiling lifts at UTC midnight — so a banner fetched once at mount would still be telling somebody they are blocked hours after an Admin lifted them. Sixty seconds is the same order as the app's other background polls and the payload is three rows.

constants.comment: Ceiling on the non-semantic branch's fetch (A1c). The branch used to be unbounded: it paged a channel's whole history into the browser and filtered there. It is now one `POST /data/posts` call, and bounding it is only sound because the server **sorts before it limits** — so `limit: N` returns the first N of the same ordering the client pipeline produced, not an arbitrary N. The one caller that reaches this branch (`useEntityFlow`'s pick-post pool) takes `.slice(0, 100)` immediately, so 200 is generous. A caller that needs more than this should page the feed (`usePostsFeed`) rather than raise the number.
